claim: Intrinsic self-correction by prompted LLMs without external feedback does not help on reasoning and often lowers accuracy; it works with reliable external feedback or after specific training.
note: Huang 2024, Kamoi 2024 survey, Kumar 2024 (SCoRe, training fix). Kamoi partly reviews Huang's literature, so independence is partial.

claim: Contested edge: self-correction may work when temperature is zero and prompts are unbiased.
note: One low-credibility preprint against the established finding.

claim: Failed self-correction is mostly a failure to locate the error, not to fix it; with the error location given, fixing works.
note: Tyen 2024. Consistent with Kamoi (external feedback works).

claim: LLMs are not reliably better at discriminating among their own answers than at generating them.
note: Jiang 2024 preprint.

claim: LLM judges recognise their own output and prefer it; self-recognition strength tracks self-preference.
note: Panickssery 2024 only; three lines are the same study. GPT-4 and Llama 2 only.

claim: Larger LMs are well calibrated on multiple-choice and true/false; P(True) improves with many own samples; trained P(IK) generalises only partly to new tasks.
note: Kadavath 2022 only, models up to 52B. Tension with Xiong: they measure token probability versus stated confidence.

claim: Verbalized confidence from black-box LLMs is overconfident; sample consistency helps; white-box beats black-box only slightly; all struggle on professional-knowledge tasks.
note: Xiong 2024 only. Direction supported by Kadavath and Farquhar.

claim: Semantic entropy detects confabulation better than P(True) or naive entropy (AUROC 0.790 vs 0.698 and 0.691) but not consistent errors.
note: Farquhar 2024, peer reviewed, strong. The limit matters: correlated samples agree on a wrong answer.

claim: Reasoning models overthink easy problems and spend tokens badly; extra thinking lowers accuracy on some tasks; at equal compute plain models win on simple puzzles, reasoning models on medium, both fail on hard; parallel paths with vote beat extended thinking.
note: Chen, Pu, Su, Liu, Ghosal, Gema, Shojaee, Cuadron. Mostly preprints, many independent groups. Matches our result that scaffolds hurt on single-answer tasks.

claim: Chain-of-thought text can be unfaithful: it often omits the real cause of the answer.
note: Turpin 2023, Chen 2025. Stated reasons are weak monitoring evidence.

claim: Monitoring and regulation dissociate in LLMs: r = .17 over 20 models; accuracy rank and metacognitive sensitivity rank largely inverted.
note: Cacioli 2026, one author, small n, preprint.

claim: A Nelson-Narens harness (feeling of knowing before, judgment after, control policy) raised Sonnet-4.6 pooled accuracy from 48.3 to 56.9.
note: Cao 2026 preprint. No cost data, pooled accuracy, one model version. A hypothesis.

claim: Indiscriminate critique degrades performance, so critique strength should vary by input.
note: MetaCrit, abstract only, preprint. Agrees in direction with Huang and our always-doubt result.

claim: Reflexion (verbal lessons stored after environment feedback) reached 91% pass@1 on HumanEval vs 80% for GPT-4.
note: Shinn 2023. Relies on external feedback (tests).

claim: Models fine-tuned to predict their own behaviour beat another model predicting them, but fail on complex and out-of-distribution tasks.
note: Binder 2024. Steyvers and Peters 2025 is a review noting human and LLM metacognition differ.

claim: A low feeling of rightness on a fluent first answer predicts more rethinking and answer change in people.
note: Thompson 2011, memory only.

claim: Warmth ratings do not separate insight from non-insight solutions; insight solutions are more often correct (57% vs 37%) yet insight errors are stickier.
note: Hedne 2016, n=51, null result against Metcalfe and Wiebe 1987. Do not gate on a self-rated closeness signal.

claim: Metacognition has an object level and a meta level linked by monitoring (up) and control (down).
note: Nelson and Narens 1990, memory. Framework, not an empirical claim.

claim: Retrieval practice beats restudy, average g about 0.50, larger with feedback.
note: Rowland 2014. Both lines are the same memory-sourced figure, never opened. Transfer to an LLM is untested.

claim: Self-explanation prompts help human learning, g about 0.55.
note: Bisra 2018, memory only.

claim: Problem solving before instruction beats instruction first for conceptual knowledge and transfer (53 studies, 166 comparisons); mostly mathematics; control design criticised.
note: Sinha and Kapur 2021 (snippet only). Ashman 2021 is a low-credibility opinion post. g about 0.36 unverified.

claim: Worked examples help novices (g about 0.48); the benefit shrinks or reverses for experienced learners (expertise reversal).
note: Kalyuga 2003 and Barbieri 2023, both memory only, kept single-source until opened.

claim: Practice testing and distributed practice are high-utility; highlighting, rereading and summarisation low-utility.
note: Dunlosky 2013, memory.

claim: Experts categorise problems by deep structure, novices by surface features.
note: Chi 1981, memory, small samples.

claim: No controlled equal-token study of productive failure, expertise reversal or desirable difficulties in LLM prompting was found.
note: Search budget ran out twice; a gap in search, not proof of absence.
